answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small, slashable bond — copper-grade collateral rather than a pearl-priced deposit — before it can transact, and bind that bond to a public, append-only reputation trellis where every peer attestation links to prior work. A sybil operator would then have to fund and age each fake identity separately, while honest agents accumulate shared history that new sock puppets cannot buy or copy, so the cost of forging many identities outruns any reward from gaming the system.
